subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Shelf Placement Science
description: A micro-lesson that makes Shelf Placement Science usable.

hook.text: Products at eye level sell 35% more than those on the bottom shelf. Same product, same price, different height.

buildup.text: Retailers charge brands for premium shelf space. Eye-level placement is prime real estate.

discovery.text: Children's cereals are placed at children's eye level. The character on the box looks downward, making eye contact.

twist.text: Store brands are on the bottom shelf not because they are worse but because premium brands paid to push them down.

climax.text: Look up and down, not just straight ahead. The best value is often on shelves you are engineered to ignore.

punchline.text: What you see first is what someone paid to put there.

quiz.question: Why are children's cereals placed lower on shelves?
options: They are lighter and easier to stock low
They are positioned at children's eye level to attract their attention
Store policy groups all cereals by brand alphabetically

details.summary: Shelf placement science positions products at eye level for maximum visibility, uses end caps for impulse attraction, and places high-margin items in the natural scanning path. Product placement determines a huge portion of what consumers actually purchase.
details.whyItMatters: Brands pay billions for premium shelf placement because position dramatically affects sales. Eye-level placement can increase sales by 35 percent.
takeaways: Eye-level placement increases product sales by roughly 35 percent
End cap displays generate eight times more sales than shelf placement
Children's products are placed at children's eye level deliberately

faq.question: Why do some brands pay for premium shelf placement?
faq.answer: Eye-level shelf space is prime real estate because shoppers naturally scan at eye height. Products placed there receive the most visual attention and sell proportionally more. Slotting fees can be millions of dollars for major retail chains.

faq.question: How do stores decide what goes where on shelves?
faq.answer: Planograms are data-driven shelf maps that optimize placement for revenue. Category managers balance brand payments for premium spots, customer flow patterns, product category logic, and margin optimization to maximize per-foot profitability.
